key_insight: A small, reproducible RNA splicing signature can identify ReNU syndrome and distinguish patients with pathogenic RNU4-2 T-loop variants from controls.
clinical_relevance: This work supports development of a quantitative biomarker to help track disease biology and test splice-targeted therapies in ReNU syndrome.
method: Analyzed RNA-seq from two independent ReNU cohorts plus controls
Filtered 483 shared splicing events and narrowed to 105 alternative 5' splice-site events
Derived a minimal six-site signature and tested it in patient iPSC-derived cortical neuron-like cells
evidence_signal: The six-site signature perfectly separated 19 n.64_65insT cases from 54 controls and produced no false positives in 5,984 additional whole-blood controls.
watch_item: The biomarker is strongest for T-loop variants and may not generalize equally well to Stem III variants or all tissues without further validation.
paper_title: A cross-tissue splicing signature as a quantitative biomarker for ReNU syndrome
